order: Make the review engine selectable through a single configuration key in the project settings file, so the choice of which engine judges a review lives in one place. Support at minimum a default engine, an alternate cross-vendor engine with a fallback to the default when the alternate is unavailable, and a dual mode where both engines review substantively and a coordinating role arbitrates between them. Keep both engines installed under one contract regardless of which is selected. Swapping that key changes only who is judging, but nothing else about the review changes. Grant the coordinating role a narrow read carve-out for the settings file itself, since read access there was never guard-blocked to begin with, so this is documented permission rather than a change to any existing guard. Update the review-routing logic to honor the setting, and document the key and the swap flow in the project's top-level documentation.
claims: The engine choice was moved into a single configuration key supporting a default engine, an alternate cross-vendor engine with fallback to the default when unavailable, and a dual mode with arbitration. Swapping the key changes only who judges, while what gets checked stays exactly the same. A narrow read carve-out for the settings file was added to existing role law, since read access there was never guard-blocked before this change. The review-routing logic and the top-level documentation were updated to match, and 2 files carried the whole change.
